title: How does Burnout Develop? Psychologist Insights with Dr Claire Plumbly

sentences.en: Psychologists, what if you could earn money beyond trading your time for money?
sentences.zh: 心理学家们，如果你们能通过出卖时间赚钱之外还能获得被动收入，会怎么样？

sentences.en: I'm Dr. Marianne Trent, clinical psychologist, and I've been developing passive and recurring income streams since 2019.
sentences.zh: 我是临床心理学家玛丽安·特伦特博士，自2019年以来，我一直在开发被动和循环收入流。

sentences.en: I have some exciting news.
sentences.zh: 我有一些令人兴奋的好消息。

sentences.en: Sophie Foote's One-to-Many programme is now open for enrolment.
sentences.zh: 苏菲·富特的“一对多”项目现在开放报名了。

sentences.en: It's designed to help you turn your expertise into scalable offers like courses, memberships and digital products.
sentences.zh: 它旨在帮助你将专业知识转化为可扩展的产品，例如课程、会员资格和数字产品。

sentences.en: I completed the programme myself in 2022 and have since supported two cohorts of psychologists through their journeys too.
sentences.zh: 我自己于2022年完成了这个项目，此后也一直支持两期心理学家走过他们的历程。

sentences.en: And if you join through my affiliate link, you'll receive Sophie's bonuses plus my own exclusive support package at no extra coSt.
sentences.zh: 如果你通过我的联盟链接加入，你将获得苏菲的奖励以及我独家提供的支持套餐，无需支付额外费用。

sentences.en: That includes six months of WhatsApp support, four group masterminds, masterclasses, personalised guidance, a Fortnum and Mason treat, and a time-limited one-to-one coaching bonus.
sentences.zh: 其中包括六个月的WhatsApp支持、四个小组智囊团、大师班、个性化指导、一份福特姆与梅森的精美礼品，以及限时的一对一教练指导奖励。

sentences.en: Enrolment closes on Monday the 16th of November at 10pm.
sentences.zh: 报名将于11月16日星期一晚上10点截止。

sentences.en: Find out more via my bonus page linked in the description.
sentences.zh: 通过简介中链接的我的奖励页面了解更多信息。

sentences.en: And remember, you must purchase through my link to receive my bonuses.
sentences.zh: 请记住，你必须通过我的链接购买才能获得我的奖励。

sentences.en: I'm here if you have any questions.
sentences.zh: 如果你有任何问题，我随时在线。

sentences.en: How would you know if you were heading towards burnout?
sentences.zh: 你将如何得知自己是否正在走向精疲力竭？

sentences.en: What would the signs and symptoms be?
sentences.zh: 会有什么迹象和症状？

sentences.en: Might other people notice before you?
sentences.zh: 其他人可能会比你更早注意到吗？

sentences.en: And once you recognise the signs and symptoms, how can you step back to make positive changes for yourself or for those that you care about?
sentences.zh: 一旦你识别出这些迹象和症状，你该如何退一步，为自己或你关心的人做出积极的改变？

sentences.en: That is the topic of this brilliant podcast episode, which is a special on burnout.
sentences.zh: 这就是这期精彩播客节目的主题，这是一期关于职业倦怠的特别节目。

sentences.en: I hope you find it so useful.
sentences.zh: 我希望你觉得它非常有用。

sentences.en: Hi, welcome along to the Aspiring Psychologist podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 嗨，欢迎来到“有志心理学家”播客。

sentences.en: I am Dr. Marianne Trent and I'm a qualified clinical psychologiSt.
sentences.zh: 我是玛丽安·特伦特博士，我是一名合格的临床心理学家。

sentences.en: Now, it's pretty on brand today that I am in my gym gear and I am off ready to go personal training.
sentences.zh: 现在，今天我穿着健身服准备去进行私人训练，这非常符合我的个人风格。

sentences.en: It's one of the things that keeps me really well.
sentences.zh: 这是让我保持良好状态的方法之一。

sentences.en: And it's one of the top tips that's mentioned towards the end of this episode, which is one of our special Burnout Bites series,
sentences.zh: 这也是本集节目快结束时提到的首要建议之一，这是我们特别的“倦怠小贴士”系列节目之一，

sentences.en: which is beautifully presented for us by Dr. Clare Plumley.
sentences.zh: 由克莱尔·普拉姆利博士为我们精彩呈现。

sentences.en: Clare is the author of a brilliant new book all about burnout and how to reduce it.
sentences.zh: 克莱尔是一本关于职业倦怠及其如何减少的新书的作者。

sentences.en: There are details in the show notes.
sentences.zh: 详细信息请参见节目简介。

sentences.en: This is episode four of the Burnout Bites series.
sentences.zh: 这是“倦怠小贴士”系列的第四集。

sentences.en: There is no need to watch them all,
sentences.zh: 你不需要把它们全部看完，

sentences.en: but they do piece together beautifully to help you to really thicken your understanding of what burnout is and how to avoid it in yourself and those that you care about or work with.
sentences.zh: 但它们完美地拼凑在一起，帮助你真正加深对什么是倦怠以及如何在自己、关心的人或同事身上避免它的理解。

sentences.en: Hopefully, we care about the people we work with too.
sentences.zh: 希望我们也同样关心我们共事的人。

sentences.en: Let's dive in and see what these stages are, how we can notice what burnout is as it develops so we can stand a chance of catching it in its tracks.
sentences.zh: 让我们深入了解这些阶段是什么，当我们注意到倦怠是如何发展的时候，以便我们有机会将它扼杀在摇篮里。

sentences.en: I will catch you on the other side.
sentences.zh: 我们在另一端见。

sentences.en: Hello and welcome back to Burnout Bites.
sentences.zh: 你好，欢迎回到“倦怠小贴士”。

sentences.en: This is episode four of a short series of six episodes designed to help you understand more about burnout so you can look after yourself and anyone in your clinical practice as well.
sentences.zh: 这是由六集组成的简短系列的第四集，旨在帮助你更多地了解倦怠，以便你也能照顾好自己和临床实践中的任何人。

sentences.en: My name is Dr. Clare Plumley and I'm a clinical psychologiSt.
sentences.zh: 我叫克莱尔·普拉姆利博士，是一名临床心理学家。

sentences.en: I specialize in trauma, anxiety and burnout and I run my own practice in Taunton, Somerset and online with a group of associates.
sentences.zh: 我专注于创伤、焦虑和职业倦怠，在萨默塞特郡汤顿以及在线上与一群同事共同运营我自己的诊所。

sentences.en: Recently, I've written a book available now.
sentences.zh: 最近，我写了一本书，现在已经上市。

sentences.en: You can link to it in the show notes.
sentences.zh: 你可以在节目简介中找到它的链接。

sentences.en: It's called Burnout, How to Manage Your Nervous System Before It Manages You.
sentences.zh: 它名为《职业倦怠：在神经系统掌控你之前如何掌控它》。

sentences.en: In today's episode, I'm going to bring you the five stage model of burnout.
sentences.zh: 在今天的节目中，我将为大家带来职业倦怠的五阶段模型。

sentences.en: Now, there are different stage models, as there are for most different concepts, different ways of understanding things, including a 12 stage model,
sentences.zh: 现在，有不同的阶段模型，就像大多数不同的概念一样，有不同的理解方式，包括一个12阶段模型，

sentences.en: which I don't talk about in my book because my mind boggles a bit if I try to wrap my head around remembering 12 stages.
sentences.zh: 我在书中没有谈到这一点，因为如果我试图在脑海中记住12个阶段，我的脑子就会有点懵。

sentences.en: I find this five stage model a really handy way of understanding it.
sentences.zh: 我发现这个五阶段模型是一个非常方便的理解方法。

sentences.en: It depicts the progression from no stress into stress, chronic stress and then tipping into burnout.
sentences.zh: 它描绘了从没有压力到产生压力、慢性压力，然后演变成职业倦怠的过程。

sentences.en: This is a model that was developed in 1980 and was first written about in a nursing magazine, an occupational nursing magazine by Robert Verninger and Dr. James Spagley.
sentences.zh: 这是一个在1980年开发的模型，最初由罗伯特·维宁格和詹姆斯·斯帕格利博士在一本护理杂志、一本职业护理杂志上撰文介绍。

sentences.en: They were trying to understand the progression from job satisfaction into job disillusionment and how this was often followed by, as they were stating in this article,
sentences.zh: 他们试图理解从工作满意度到工作幻灭感的转变，以及正如他们在本文中所述，这通常伴随着什么，

sentences.en: physical and mental health difficulties, which then just swamp and overwhelm the individual.
sentences.zh: 身体和心理健康困难，这些困难随后会压垮和淹没个人。

sentences.en: It's a fairly well-referenced model in regards to burnout these days.
sentences.zh: 如今，关于职业倦怠，这是一个引用率相当高的模型。

sentences.en: Hold in mind that stage models can oversimplify things and they can suggest a linear trajectory through each stage into the next one.
sentences.zh: 请记住，阶段模型可能会过于简单化，并且它们可能暗示通过每个阶段进入下一个阶段的线性轨迹。

sentences.en: And often we might oscillate between them, but I'm sure you would have that awareness of stage models anyway.
sentences.zh: 通常我们可能会在它们之间摇摆不定，但我相信你无论如何都会对阶段模型有所了解。

sentences.en: So stage one is the honeymoon stage.
sentences.zh: 所以第一阶段是蜜月期。

sentences.en: I'm going to go through each stage and I'm going to explain what it is and the signs that you might be here.
sentences.zh: 我将经历每个阶段，并解释它是什么以及你可能处于此阶段的迹象。

sentences.en: And then we can think at the end of this episode about what you might need to do at each point.
sentences.zh: 然后我们可以在本集节目结束时思考你在每个阶段可能需要做些什么。

sentences.en: Stage, you generally feel pretty satisfied with what you're doing and achieving.
sentences.zh: 在这个阶段，你通常对自己的所作所为和成就感到非常满意。

sentences.en: Energy levels and enthusiasm might be high.
sentences.zh: 能量水平和热情可能很高。

sentences.en: So you're driven, maybe enthusiastic, and you wouldn't necessarily think of yourself as potentially burning out because you don't have any of the signs of distress.
sentences.zh: 所以你很有动力，也许很热情，你不会认为自己可能会精疲力竭，因为你没有任何痛苦的迹象。

sentences.en: So actually you're not burning out right now.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上你现在并没有精疲力竭。

sentences.en: However, it's important to know about this stage because you can prevent yourself progressing to the next one with some gentle interventions.
sentences.zh: 然而，了解这个阶段很重要，因为你可以通过一些温和的干预措施来防止自己进入下一个阶段。

sentences.en: I tend to notice when I'm like this, I'm really struggling to pace myself.
sentences.zh: 我往往会注意到，当我处于这种状态时，我真的很挣扎于控制自己的节奏。

sentences.en: I'm often very, very excited by projects and I'm saying yes to everything because I want a bite of every pie.
sentences.zh: 我经常对项目感到非常非常兴奋，我对一切都说“好”，因为我想尝遍每个派。

sentences.en: So you'll recognize you're here if you feel any of what I've just described, that kind of enthusiasm.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你感觉到我刚才描述的任何内容，那种热情，你就会认出你在这里。

sentences.en: You're saying yes to too many things.
sentences.zh: 你对太多事情说“好”。

sentences.en: You're kind of excited and rushing and you're feeling really positive about outcomes, not really think about the practicalities of about how you will reach them.
sentences.zh: 你有点兴奋和冲动，对结果感觉非常积极，并没有真正考虑如何实现这些结果的实际问题。

sentences.en: You might also start to drop other things in the pursuit of these goals.
sentences.zh: 为了追求这些目标，你可能还会开始放弃其他事情。

sentences.en: So for example, your boring admin, life admin, hobbies or social connections, and maybe your boundaries between work and life start to get blurred.
sentences.zh: 例如，你的枯燥行政工作、生活行政事务、爱好或社交关系，也许你的工作与生活之间的界限开始变得模糊。

sentences.en: So for example, when I was doing my studying to become a psychologist, often I found at every moment of the day I had a workbook in my bag to pull out and read.
sentences.zh: 例如，当我学习成为一名心理学家时，我经常发现一天中的每一刻我的包里都有一本练习册可以拿出来阅读。

sentences.en: And these days, of course, we have our phones with us, we can easily dip into reading something or checking emails.
sentences.zh: 当然，现在我们随身携带手机，我们可以轻松地开始阅读某些内容或查看电子邮件。

sentences.en: So all of this feels kind of almost easy and like you really wanted to get into work.
sentences.zh: 因此，所有这一切感觉几乎很容易，就像你真的很想投入工作一样。

sentences.en: And so boundaries are very hard to kind of hold in place.
sentences.zh: 因此，界限很难保持在原位。

sentences.en: Stage two, this is the onset of stress.
sentences.zh: 第二阶段，这是压力的开始。

sentences.en: So projects might start to lose their shine as the reality of the demands start to kick in.
sentences.zh: 因此，随着需求的现实开始显现，项目可能开始失去光彩。

sentences.en: So there are some very common external stresses at this point that might highlight this stage as being relevant to you.
sentences.zh: 因此，此时有一些非常常见的外部压力源，可能会突出显示此阶段与你相关。

sentences.en: So this is when we might notice having too much to do or that we're being deprived of having agency, choosing how we want to do those things.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是我们可能会注意到有太多事情要做，或者我们被剥夺了自主权，无法选择我们希望如何做这些事情的时候。

sentences.en: So our choice feels curtailed.
sentences.zh: 所以我们的选择感觉受到限制。

sentences.en: You might feel criticised or like your efforts aren't actually being rewarded or appreciated.
sentences.zh: 你可能会感到受到批评，或者觉得你的努力实际上没有得到回报或赞赏。

sentences.en: Could feel like you're being unfairly treated or that you're unsupported in everything you're doing.
sentences.zh: 可能会觉得你受到了不公平的对待，或者你在所做的每件事上都得不到支持。

sentences.en: If you don't have any buffers to stress in place, which of course, if you remember in stage one, might have gone.
sentences.zh: 如果你没有采取任何应对压力的缓冲措施，当然，如果你还记得第一阶段，这些措施可能已经消失了。

sentences.en: If you're not having those boundaries and that downtime, those social connections, then your body might start to react even more with the stress responses.
sentences.zh: 如果你没有这些界限、停机时间和社交联系，那么你的身体可能会对压力反应做出更多的反应。

sentences.en: So signs that you are here, you're getting more irritable or impatient on issues that are pretty minor,
sentences.zh: 因此，你身处此地的迹象是，你在一些相当小的问题上变得更加易怒或不耐烦，

sentences.en: like being asked a favour or someone's walking too slowly or my classic is when I'm queuing.
sentences.zh: 比如被要求帮个忙，或者有人走路太慢，或者我的经典例子是我在排队的时候。

sentences.en: Your brain might start to race or you might start to find the worries are really hard to dismiss.
sentences.zh: 你的大脑可能会开始飞速运转，或者你可能会发现担忧真的很难打消。

sentences.en: You might find it hard to switch off.
sentences.zh: 你可能会发现很难关机。

sentences.en: So you might want to rest or sleep, but you're finding that really challenging to do.
sentences.zh: 所以你可能想休息或睡觉，但你发现这真的很难做到。

sentences.en: And as before, you're neglecting things, maybe your personal needs.
sentences.zh: 和以前一样，你忽略了事情，也许是你的个人需求。

sentences.en: You're finding it hard to tune into your stress, maybe rushing around and not really noticing how tense or overwhelmed you're beginning to feel.
sentences.zh: 你发现很难适应你的压力，也许四处奔波，并没有真正注意到你开始感到多么紧张或不知所措。

sentences.en: Stage three.
sentences.zh: 第三阶段。

sentences.en: This is chronic stress.
sentences.zh: 这是慢性压力。

sentences.en: So your initial stress isn't addressed.
sentences.zh: 所以你最初的压力没有得到解决。

sentences.en: If your initial stress feeling isn't addressed, the longer lasting physical impacts of stress start to take their toll.
sentences.zh: 如果你最初的压力感没有得到解决，压力的长期身体影响就会开始显现。

sentences.en: So you might start to notice even more signs that you are in that fight or flight part of your nervous system.
sentences.zh: 因此，你可能会开始注意到更多迹象，表明你处于神经系统的那个战斗或逃跑部分。

sentences.en: So you're overreacting really quickly with anxiety or annoyance.
sentences.zh: 所以你对焦虑或烦恼的反应非常快。

sentences.en: You might have even panic attacks or bouts of irritability or just feeling almost paralysed and frozen.
sentences.zh: 你甚至可能会惊恐发作、易怒发作，或者感觉几乎瘫痪和冻结。

sentences.en: You might get physical signs, you know, headaches, back pain.
sentences.zh: 你可能会出现身体症状，你知道的，头痛、背痛。

sentences.en: You might start catching colds more easily or have reduced libido.
sentences.zh: 你可能会更容易感冒或性欲减退。

sentences.en: And the cognitive signs of this, difficulty making decisions, difficulty focusing or concentrating or something.
sentences.zh: 以及这方面的认知迹象，难以做出决定，难以集中注意力或专心致志之类的。

sentences.en: So classic is going into a room, forgetting why you're there, being halfway through a task and getting distracted, moving on.
sentences.zh: 所以经典的例子是走进一个房间，忘记你在那里做什么，进行了一半的任务却分心了，继续前进。

sentences.en: So you have lots of unfinished tasks.
sentences.zh: 所以你有很多未完成的任务。

sentences.en: And your coping for stress that's unhealthy might be more obvious at this point.
sentences.zh: 在这个时候，你对不健康的压力的应对可能会更加明显。

sentences.en: So classic for me might be doom scrolling, procrastinating, seeking more reassurance, like checking in with my other half or with colleagues, like if everything's okay.
sentences.zh: 所以对我的经典来说可能是厄运滚动、拖延、寻求更多的安慰，比如向我的另一半或同事核对，比如一切是否都还好。

sentences.en: And as I mentioned in a previous episode, a classic for me is also impulse online shopping, of course.
sentences.zh: 正如我在前一集里提到的，对我来说，另一个经典当然是冲动网购。

sentences.en: But that might look different for different people.
sentences.zh: 但这对于不同的人来说可能看起来有所不同。

sentences.en: I also tend to find that I go into a bit of a zone out place where I'm, it's also very common to really struggle to switch your body into a mode where you can reSt.
sentences.zh: 我也往往发现我进入了一种有点脱离现实的状态，在那里，也很难让你的身体进入可以休息的模式。

sentences.en: So this can lead to real extra difficulties falling asleep or staying asleep.
sentences.zh: 这会导致入睡或保持睡眠出现真正的额外困难。

sentences.en: Many people find it really hard to admit to themselves just how stressed they are.
sentences.zh: 许多人发现很难向自己承认自己有多大压力。

sentences.en: Stage four is when we actually reach burnout.
sentences.zh: 第四阶段是我们真正达到倦怠的时候。

sentences.en: But in my mind, this is high functioning burnout.
sentences.zh: 但在我看来，这是高功能职业倦怠。

sentences.en: So you might be able to still do all the things that you normally do, but you're starting to feel just wrung out.
sentences.zh: 所以你可能仍然能够做你通常做的所有事情，但你开始觉得筋疲力尽。

sentences.en: So perhaps decisions just feel almost like overwhelming, like you just can't make any.
sentences.zh: 所以也许决定几乎让人不知所措，好像你根本无法做出任何决定。

sentences.en: And this could be simple things like what to have for dinner or whether you're going to attend something or not.
sentences.zh: 这可能是简单的事情，比如晚饭吃什么，或者你是否要参加某项活动。

sentences.en: You might also find that you're comparing yourself unfavorably to others.
sentences.zh: 你可能还会发现自己将自己与他人进行不利的比较。

sentences.en: So this is that difficulty with personal accomplishment.
sentences.zh: 这就是个人成就感的困难所在。

sentences.en: We tend to assume that others are looking down at us.
sentences.zh: 我们往往认为别人在看不起我们。

sentences.en: We feel less able and confident in our abilities.
sentences.zh: 我们对自己的能力感到不如以前有能力和自信。

sentences.en: And we can't identify with others who are really at the same level as us because they just feel like they're on a different planet.
sentences.zh: 我们无法认同那些真正和我们处于同一水平的人，因为他们感觉就像在不同的星球上一样。

sentences.en: So again, all the same signs here as the stress before.
sentences.zh: 同样，这里的核心标志与之前的压力完全相同。

sentences.en: But everything, if you imagine your body is kind of whispering to you before, everything's dialed up.
sentences.zh: 但一切，如果你想象你的身体之前在对你耳语，现在一切都被调大了。

sentences.en: So those aches and pains and niggles are harder to distract yourself from.
sentences.zh: 因此，那些酸痛和疼痛以及小毛病更难让你转移注意力。

sentences.en: You might be feeling even more, you might be noticing even more frequent and louder types of negative thoughts
sentences.zh: 你可能会感到更多，你可能会注意到更频繁、更响亮的消极想法

sentences.en: about how critical you are of yourself, your abilities, about others not being there for you, feeling unable to reach out for that support.
sentences.zh: 关于你对你自己、你的能力的挑剔，关于别人不在你身边，感到无法伸出援手寻求支持。

sentences.en: You might be making more mistakes.
sentences.zh: 你可能会犯更多的错误。

sentences.en: So cognitively, you're less sharp and efficient and able.
sentences.zh: 所以在认知上，你的敏锐度、效率和能力都有所下降。

sentences.en: You might be forgetting to do things or ordering the wrong iteMs.
sentences.zh: 你可能会忘记做事或订购错误的物品。

sentences.en: This is where you might also begin to feel really cynical or resentful towards others or the work you're being asked to do.
sentences.zh: 这也是你开始对他人或被要求做的工作感到真正愤世嫉俗或怨恨的时候。

sentences.en: Mood can also drop.
sentences.zh: 情绪也可能会下降。

sentences.en: So you might begin to feel really trapped, unable to imagine how to break free.
sentences.zh: 所以你可能会开始感到真正的被困住，无法想象如何打破束缚。

sentences.en: This is where you get those escapism thoughts about how you could actually escape from what you're doing.
sentences.zh: 这就是你产生逃避想法的地方，关于你如何真正逃离你正在做的事情。

sentences.en: Now, transition points in the day are often a good marker of this.
sentences.zh: 现在，一天中的过渡点通常是这方面的一个很好的标志。

sentences.en: If you think about the moment you finish doing something like for me when I'm closing my computer down to go and get the kids from school,
sentences.zh: 如果你想想你完成某事的那一刻，比如对我来说，当我关闭电脑去学校接孩子时，

sentences.en: that's a classic transition where I really notice this.
sentences.zh: 这是一个我真正注意到这一点的典型过渡。

sentences.en: You know, I've been in a mode where I'm trying to do thinking, access kind of clever thought stuff from writing or working on something.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我一直处于一种试图思考的状态，从写作或处理某事中获取某种聪明的思维东西。

sentences.en: And then I've got to kind of go drive, get the kids.
sentences.zh: 然后我得去开车接孩子。

sentences.en: And I often find I have a telltale sign that I'm in this kind of stage of burnout when I get to the school and feel really irritable,
sentences.zh: 我经常发现，当我到达学校并感到非常烦躁时，我有一个明显的迹象表明我正处于这种倦怠阶段，

sentences.en: unable to really connect with where I am and what I'm doing.
sentences.zh: 无法真正与我在哪里以及我在做什么建立联系。

sentences.en: So the kids might be asking me very reasonable questions about, you know, what we're doing after school.
sentences.zh: 所以孩子们可能会问我非常合理的问题，你知道的，放学后我们要去哪里。

sentences.en: And I kind of feel like they're annoying little flies buzzing around me, but really in my own head.
sentences.zh: 我有点觉得他们是烦人的小苍蝇在我身边嗡嗡叫，但实际上在我自己的脑子里。

sentences.en: So this transition point is maybe something for you to think about as well.
sentences.zh: 所以这个过渡点也许也是你可以考虑的事情。

sentences.en: You struggling to initiate the next activity efficiently.
sentences.zh: 你难以高效地开始下一个活动。

sentences.en: You know, this could be starting or finishing work, but it could either be other things like mealtimes or when you put the kids to bed.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这可能是开始或结束工作，但它也可能是其他事情，比如用餐时间或你让孩子上床睡觉的时候。

sentences.en: So that's another time for me, you know, rather than sitting and feeling like I can snuggle with them and read.
sentences.zh: 所以对我来说这是另一个时间，你知道的，而不是坐着感觉我可以和他们依偎在一起阅读。

sentences.en: I feel like irritable that I just want to get through bedtime really quickly and I'm not able to really engage with it.
sentences.zh: 我觉得很烦躁，我只想快点度过就寝时间，而且我无法真正参与其中。

sentences.en: The final thing I just want to add to this as a sign is that you might feel really alone with all of this as well.
sentences.zh: 我想补充的最后一件事作为一个迹象是，你可能也会对这一切感到非常孤独。

sentences.en: So hold on to that feeling.
sentences.zh: 所以抓住那种感觉。

sentences.en: Right, number five, we've got habitual burnout now.
sentences.zh: 好的，第五号，我们现在有了习惯性倦怠。

sentences.en: This is the burnout that is much more established and set in.
sentences.zh: 这是更加成熟和根深蒂固的职业倦怠。

sentences.en: All those signs of distress might be really shouting at you now.
sentences.zh: 现在所有那些痛苦的迹象可能都在对你大喊大叫。

sentences.en: And clinical burnout is when your body just forces that stop.
sentences.zh: 临床倦怠是你的身体强行叫停的时候。

sentences.en: It's been asking and begging you to stop and you haven't.
sentences.zh: 它一直在请求和乞求你停下来，而你没有。

sentences.en: And so now it just says, uh-uh, I'm not proceeding anymore.
sentences.zh: 所以现在它只是说，不，我不再前进了。

sentences.en: So you might have this experience of struggling to get out of bed.
sentences.zh: 所以你可能会有这种难以起床的经历。

sentences.en: I've also worked with people who have had non-epileptic attack disorder, so seizures that aren't explained by epilepsy, or panic attacks that just completely floor them.
sentences.zh: 我也曾与患有非癫痫性发作障碍的人合作过，也就是无法用癫痫解释的发作，或者彻底击垮他们的惊恐发作。

sentences.en: I've also had people who haven't been able to speak, who struggle to find words or actually talk.
sentences.zh: 我遇到过一些甚至无法说话、艰难寻找词汇或开口交谈的人。

sentences.en: So there could be all sorts of different, very intense physical signs of stress.
sentences.zh: 所以可能会出现各种各样、非常强烈的身体压力信号。

sentences.en: And this is when often people are signed off work sick for a period of time.
sentences.zh: 这也是人们通常会因病请假一段时间的时候。

sentences.en: So I hope the message is coming across from this stage model that it's more helpful to think of burnout on a continuum rather than a I either have it or I don't type of concept.
sentences.zh: 所以我希望这个阶段模型传达的信息是，把职业倦怠看作是一个连续体，而不是“我有”或“我没有”这种非黑即白的观念，会更有帮助。

sentences.en: What we use to continuums in psychology, so I'm sure this isn't a new idea.
sentences.zh: 我们在心理学中习惯了连续体，所以我确信这并不是一个新概念。

sentences.en: The important thing is to think about what you need at each stage.
sentences.zh: 重要的是思考你在每个阶段需要什么。

sentences.en: Really early on when you don't have any signs of burnout but you're not pacing yourself, this is something to think about.
sentences.zh: 在非常早期的时候，当你还没有任何倦怠迹象，但又没有把握好节奏，这就是需要思考的问题。

sentences.en: This boom-bust pattern is really common for people.
sentences.zh: 这种“爆发-崩溃”的模式对人们来说非常普遍。

sentences.en: What can you do to prevent this happening?
sentences.zh: 你能做些什么来防止这种情况发生？

sentences.en: Are there people in your team, you know, a partner, a colleague who can help you stay in check?
sentences.zh: 你的团队里有没有人，比如伴侣或同事，能够帮你在自我检查时把好关？

sentences.en: So for example, my husband knows I get like this and he's often the one saying, have you thought about X?
sentences.zh: 比如，我丈夫知道我有时会这样，他经常是那个问我“你考虑过X吗？”的人。

sentences.en: So often just asking me that question.
sentences.zh: 所以往往只需要问我这个问题。

sentences.en: We've got this agreement that he will do this for me.
sentences.zh: 我们达成了这样的协议，他会为我这么做。

sentences.en: It helps me to kind of check myself out.
sentences.zh: 这帮我能够自我审视一番。

sentences.en: Actually, I'm not going to have time to say, do all these things I'm saying yes to.
sentences.zh: 实际上，我根本没有时间去答应并且做完我所承诺的所有事情。

sentences.en: So pacing yourself and then also making sure you've got things in your diary that you just focus on and prioritise even when you don't feel like doing it for your self-care.
sentences.zh: 因此，把握好节奏，同时确保你的日程表里有一些即使你不想做、为了自我关怀也必须专注于并优先处理的事情。

sentences.en: So that might be the exercise class.
sentences.zh: 那可能是一个锻炼班。

sentences.en: It might be a telephone call with a friend.
sentences.zh: 可能是一个和朋友的通电话。

sentences.en: Making sure that these, even if they're just shorter, you're still doing something along those lines.
sentences.zh: 确保这些事情，即使时间较短，你仍然在朝着这个方向去做。

sentences.en: Because those are the things that are going to keep you protected and they help you keep perspective as well.
sentences.zh: 因为这些是能够保护你并帮助你保持清醒认识的事情。

sentences.en: Because when we just throw ourselves into work, we do more and more work.
sentences.zh: 因为当我们一头扎进工作时，我们会做越来越多的工作。

sentences.en: That perspective is really hard to hold on to.
sentences.zh: 那种宏观视角真的很难保持。

sentences.en: Of course, later up the stages, two, three and four.
sentences.zh: 当然，再往后就是第二、第三和第四阶段了。

sentences.en: This is all where we need to tend to our physiology, tend to our nervous system to keep it soothed and managed.
sentences.zh: 这些都是我们需要关注自己的生理机能、照顾神经系统以使其保持舒缓和管理的状态。

sentences.en: And little pockets throughout the day are the best time to do that.
sentences.zh: 而全天的一些零散时间是做到这一点的最佳时机。

sentences.en: So I'm going to focus on that in the next episode with you.
sentences.zh: 所以我将在下一集中与大家重点探讨这一点。

sentences.en: In the final stage of burnout, this is where you need a proper break from work.
sentences.zh: 在职业倦怠的最后阶段，这就是你需要好好休息一下的时候。

sentences.en: If you can set things up or ask someone to help you set up, getting everything delegated so that you're not having to do things anymore.
sentences.zh: 如果你能做好安排，或者请人帮你安排，把所有事情都委派出去，这样你就不用再亲自动手了。

sentences.en: Often if people are off work, that starts to happen anyway.
sentences.zh: 通常如果人们请假离开工作，情况无论如何都会开始朝着这个方向发展。

sentences.en: But it is trickier if your burnout is linked to being a student or being at home with your family.
sentences.zh: 但如果你的倦怠与身为学生或在家照顾家人有关，情况就会更棘手一些。

sentences.en: It's important to let people know that you're not able to do all of the usual activities and tasks that you usually are able to.
sentences.zh: 重要的是让大家知道，你无法像平时那样完成所有常规的活动和任务。

sentences.en: It takes time to recover from clinical burnout where your body is forced to stop.
sentences.zh: 从身体被迫停下来的临床职业倦怠中恢复需要时间。

sentences.en: This is highly traumatic for the body and it also can be traumatic for you to have this idea that I'm not infallible.
sentences.zh: 这对身体来说是高度创伤性的，而且对于让你接受“并非万无一失”这一观念来说，也可能是一种创伤。

sentences.en: I do have a pause point where I can't go beyond.
sentences.zh: 我的确有一个无法超越的极限点。

sentences.en: So you need to be really gentle with yourself at this point and encourage other people around you to learn about burnout so that they can be gentle with you too.
sentences.zh: 所以在这一点上，你必须对自我非常温柔，并鼓励你周围的人了解职业倦怠，这样他们也能对你温柔以待。

sentences.en: You don't want to be trying to do this all on your own.
sentences.zh: 你可不想独自一人去面对这一切。

sentences.en: Maybe they could read my book.
sentences.zh: 也许他们可以读读我的书。

sentences.en: That might be helpful for them to understand it so that they can support you.
sentences.zh: 这可能有助于他们理解，以便他们能够支持你。

sentences.en: This brings us to the end of this episode.
sentences.zh: 这就来到了本集的尾声。

sentences.en: We're going to go a little more into detail in the practicalities of pacing and how to do that in the transition points of your day in the next episode.
sentences.zh: 在下一集中，我们将更详细地探讨把握节奏的实际操作方法，以及如何在一天中的过渡时刻做到这一点。

sentences.en: So come back to episode five for more on this.
sentences.zh: 所以请收看第五集，了解更多内容。

sentences.en: Oh gosh, thank you so much, Dr. Claire.
sentences.zh: 哦天哪，非常感谢你，克莱尔博士。

sentences.en: How wonderful to have that broken down into those stages that makes it so accessible and so memorable so that we can start to notice what our patterns are.
sentences.zh: 能把这些分解成不同的阶段真是太棒了，这让它变得如此通俗易懂、令人难忘，从而让我们能够开始注意到自己的模式是什么。

sentences.en: But I love the idea of giving people permission in your world to help you stay on track to keep you as well as possible.
sentences.zh: 但我很喜欢这个想法：在你的世界里允许别人帮助你保持正轨，让你尽可能保持健康。

sentences.en: And I absolutely resonate with some of that kind of run out of window of tolerance stuff.
sentences.zh: 而且我绝对能对那种“容忍窗口耗尽”的说法产生共鸣。

sentences.en: And I absolutely resonate with some of that running out of patience and tolerance at the end of the day and not being able to fully immerse myself in what can be quite a special time putting my children to bed.
sentences.zh: 我完全感同身受那种在一天结束时耐心和包容心耗尽的感觉，无法全身心地投入到哄孩子睡觉这段本应非常特殊的时光中。

sentences.en: Sometimes I'm just like, I just need you gone.
sentences.zh: 有时我只是想：我真希望你们赶紧消失。

sentences.en: I just need you in bed so that I can just sit and kind of decompress a bit.
sentences.zh: 我只想让你们快点上床睡觉，这样我就可以坐下来稍微放松和减压一下。

sentences.en: I would love to know what this episode has evoked for you.
sentences.zh: 我很想知道这一集引发了你怎样的感触。
